To the best of our knowledge, this is the first application of a vision FM to near real time (NRT) the 7 km TROPOMI SO2 product for volcano monitoring. Experimental results obtained on a dataset of 100 volcanic SO2 plume images show that the proposed framework achieves an average intersection over union (IoU) of 0.655 and an  $F1$ -score of 0.768, demonstrating its effectiveness for automatic plume segmentation across diverse volcanic scenarios. These results highlight the potential of generalist vision FMs for scalable and automated analysis of volcanic emissions and underscore their suitability for real-time geospatial monitoring applications.
author: Simona Cariello, Claudia Corradino, Alessandro La Spina, Ciro Del Negro

title: Global Daily XCO2 Reconstruction at 0.05° Resolution for 2021–2024 Using Satellite and Reanalysis Data
content: Accurate and seamless reconstruction of column-averaged dry-air CO2 mole fraction (XCO ${}_{2}$ ) at high spatial and temporal resolution remains challenging because satellite observations are sparse, unevenly distributed, and frequently interrupted by clouds and retrieval-related limitations. In this study, we propose Trans-XCO2, a spatiotemporal deep learning (DL) framework for reconstructing global daily XCO2 at 0.05° resolution during 2021–2024 by integrating transport background fields with multisource environmental predictors. The framework incorporates instantaneous environmental covariates and short-term atmospheric memory to represent temporal transport effects, and uses a wavelet-enhanced Transformer (WET) to improve multiscale spatial representation. A dual-resolution decoding strategy is further introduced to preserve large-scale background structures while refining fine-scale spatial details. The model is trained using data from 2021 to 2023 and evaluated through strict temporal extrapolation in 2024. Independent validation against measurements from the Total Carbon Column Observing Network (TCCON) shows strong agreement, with an R2 of 0.93 and an RMSE of 1.04 ppm. Compared with coarse-resolution background products, Trans-XCO2 achieves lower reconstruction errors while better preserving spatial gradients. The reconstructed dataset reveals a persistent global XCO2 growth rate of approximately 2.36 ppm yr−1 during 2021–2024, with similar temporal trends over land and ocean. The resulting seamless high-resolution XCO2 dataset provides valuable support for atmospheric carbon monitoring, satellite-model data fusion, and carbon cycle analysis.
author: Zhao Meng, Juepeng Zheng, Yuting Zhu, Haohuan Fu

title: A Rapid Multibeam Water Column Data Mapping Method Based on Pixel-Level Interpolation Templates
content: Multibeam water column data serve as a crucial data source for achieving high-precision underwater terrain and environmental detection. However, existing data visualization methods face significant bottlenecks in terms of both real-time performance and post-processing efficiency. Currently, multibeam water column data are typically acquired in a polar coordinate system but require conversion to a Cartesian coordinate system for visualization. This process involves extensive coordinate transformations and interpolation operations, resulting in high computational complexity. The inefficiency of data mapping has limited its practical application in engineering projects. To address this issue, in this article, the performance limitations of traditional interpolation algorithms in water column data mapping are systematically analyzed. On the basis of the distribution characteristics of water column data, a pixel-level template-based rapid mapping method that leverages the distribution characteristics of water column data is proposed. This approach extracts repetitive computational steps during the mapping process of data from the same survey line and abstracts them into a unified pixel-level template, effectively reducing the search and computational overhead during mapping and significantly lowering the algorithm’s time complexity. Furthermore, to address common factors affecting practical operations, such as vessel roll compensation, a dynamic adjustment and optimization mechanism for the template is introduced, enhancing the algorithm’s adaptability and robustness in complex scenarios. The proposed method was validated using both simulated data and real-measured data, covering typical shallow-water and deep-sea application environments. Compared with the conventional interpolation algorithm, the proposed method improves the data mapping efficiency by 11–142 times while maintaining the imaging quality. This advancement not only meets the demands of real-time processing but also provides effective technical support for larger-scale and higher-density water column data acquisition, demonstrating significant engineering application value.
author: Jianbing Chen, Ziyin Wu, Fanlin Yang, Mingwei Wang, Xianhai Bu, Dineng Zhao, Jihong Shang, Jieqiong Zhou, Yang Liu

title: The PID-Aware Geometric Semantic Representation Learning for Infrared-Visible Image Fusion
content: To relieve the problems of the lack of semantic alignment in the geometric representation space and insufficient modality-specific instruction calibration in infrared-visible image fusion (IVIF), we first propose a dynamic instruction-aware geometric representation (DIGR) for IVIF, which achieves semantic alignment between fusion features and semantic features within the geometric space and progressively injects textual instructions into the deep-layer features. Second, to alleviate the semantic gap between fusion features and semantic features, we propose a cross-graph neighborhood interaction (CGNI) module. In this module, each node in one graph is updated by aggregating information from the neighbor nodes of its position-aligned counterpart in the other graph, thereby enabling cross-level semantic alignment. Third, to alleviate the absence of modality-related text correction in the fusion network, we introduce an instruction-guided proportional–integral–derivative (IPID) calibration module, which uses modality-aware texts as external priors. By modeling the discrepancy between instructions and deep-level modality features using the proportional–integral–derivative (PID) control principle, IPID achieves progressive and controllable instruction calibration. Extensive experiments on three public datasets, namely, MFNet, Potsdam, and WHU, demonstrate that the proposed DIGR achieves superior fusion results and segmentation performance. The code of DIGR is publicly available at https://github.com/YongzheWang666/DIGR
author: Mengru Ma, Yongzhe Wang, Wenping Ma, Licheng Jiao, Lingling Li, Xu Liu, Fang Liu

title: Exploring Canopy Emissivity Over Sloping Terrains
content: Topography is an inevitable influencing factor for remote sensing observations. Studies have shown that ignoring topographic effects induces significant errors in radiative transfer simulations and surface parameter estimates. However, topographic effects on surface emissivity have not been well studied or given much attention, especially in soil-vegetation systems, because of the complicated, combined effects of gravitropism and topography. This study first derives an emissivity model from the 4SAILT, which was developed based on the well-known scattering by arbitrary inclined leaves (4SAIL) model and considers topographic and gravitropic effects. Then, the significance of topography, gravitropism, leaf angle distribution (LAD), and soil anisotropy in canopy emissivity is analyzed. Finally, an algorithm for retrieving land surface emissivity (LSE) and land surface temperature (LST) that considers topographic and gravitropic effects was proposed. An evaluation of the emissivity model via Monte Carlo simulations provided by the Discrete Anisotropic Radiative Transfer (DART) model demonstrated its accuracy, with a root-mean-squared difference (RMSD) of 0.0008 and a normalized RMSD (NRMSD) of 4.72% for  $r$ -emissivity and an RMSD of 0.0006 and a NRMSD of 4.30% for  $e$ -emissivity. The results prove that, unlike on horizontal surfaces, the surface emissivity of sloping terrain is no longer identical across azimuth angles due to topography and gravitropism. Furthermore, the analysis shows that: 1) ignoring topography induces significant errors in surface emissivity, with NRMSDs of 7.5%–64.8%; 2) ignoring gravitropism results an overall NRMSD of 1.3%–15.7%, and its influence is still significant even for sparse vegetation over steep slopes; 3) the spherical LAD assumption induces an error in emissivity up to 0.004; thus, should be cautious to be adopted; and 4) soil anisotropy has mutual effects with topography and LAD on surface emissivity, and an error up to 18.6% is observed if neglecting soil anisotropy. In particular, the significance of soil anisotropy increases in mountainous areas, even in areas covered with dense vegetation. The importance of topography in mountainous areas is also demonstrated from the perspective of surface emissivity and temperature inversion. A preliminary sensitivity test on an Advanced Spaceborne Thermal Emission and Reflection Radiometer (ASTER) image shows that ignoring the combined influence of topography, plant gravitropism, and the cavity effect results in a mean difference (MD) of −0.006 to −0.013 for emissivity and 0.346 K for temperature. This study demonstrates the significance of topography for surface emissivity and highlights its interactions with other influencing factors. The ready-to-use emissivity model and inversion algorithm, along with the findings presented in this work, could potentially benefit thermal remote sensing studies in mountainous areas. However, it is noted that they were developed from solo-slope theory, and their practical applicability over rugged terrains must be further carefully evaluated based on a digital elevation model (DEM) of the study areas.
author: Hanyu Shi

title: Satellite Topographic Mapping in Complex Intertidal Wetlands: A Canopy-Height-Constrained Fusion of ICESat-2 Photon-Derived Structural Samples and Single-Phase Submeter Optical Imagery
content: High-resolution topographic mapping of intertidal wetlands is essential for geomorphic analysis, yet existing remote sensing methods often struggle with vegetation interference, dependence on dense time-series data, and limited representation of fine geomorphic features. We propose a canopy-height-constrained stratified cooperative inversion framework for the entire intertidal wetland, integrating single-phase submeter optical imagery (Jilin-1), spaceborne photon-counting light detection and ranging (LiDAR) Ice, Cloud, and Land Elevation Satellite 2 (ICESat-2), and machine learning. To accurately construct digital elevation model (DEM) and canopy height model (CHM) training samples in salt-marsh environments, we developed an ATL03 photon-classification workflow combining histogram-based control-point extraction and morphological refinement to generate these samples directly from ICESat-2 ATL03 photons. The retrieved CHM was then introduced as a structural constraint in the DEM retrieval model to support canopy-terrain signal decoupling in vegetated salt-marsh areas. A case study on Chongming Island, Shanghai, China, demonstrated that the DEM retrieval achieved high accuracy on the test set (R ${}^{2} =0.94$ , root-mean-squared error (RMSE) = 0.28 m) and maintained consistent performance against independent UAV-LiDAR validation data (R ${}^{2} = 0.53-0.77$  and RMSE = 0.34–0.53 m). The retrieved 0.5-m DEM reproduced regional elevation gradients, tidal-creek networks, and microtopographic variations across bare flats and vegetated marshes. Shapley additive explanation (SHAP) analysis showed that elevation retrieval over bare mudflats relied mainly on spectral predictors, whereas vegetated areas exhibited a complementary spectral-texture-CHM structure, with CHM consistently ranking as a mid-to-high predictor (fourth–seventh). This further supports the role of CHM as an effective structural constraint. By using only single-phase imagery and ATL03-derived DEM/CHM samples, the framework enables intertidal topographic retrieval that includes vegetated areas. It therefore provides an efficient and low-cost pathway for high-accuracy intertidal topographic monitoring under complex environmental conditions and limited image availability.
author: Zhenjie Yang, Weiwei Sun, Jianrong Zhu, Tao Zheng, Gang Yang, Chao Sun, Wenxiang Ji, Weiguo Zhang, Nan Xu, Chunpeng Chen, Weiming Xie, Qingji Huang, Kai Tan

title: Unsupervised Class-Guided Synthetic-to-Real Domain Adaptation for Plot-Level Forest UAV LiDAR Semantic Segmentation
content: Semantic segmentation of forest point clouds is pivotal for automated forest inventory but is severely constrained by the scarcity of high-quality real-world annotations. Although synthetic forest point clouds provide a scalable alternative for training, models trained on synthetic data often suffer from pronounced performance degradation when transferred to real forest scenes, due to domain shifts coupled with extreme structural heterogeneity and long-tailed semantic distributions. To address these challenges, we propose ForestPlotUDA, an unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) framework specifically designed for plot-level forest UAV light detection and ranging (LiDAR) semantic segmentation. Unlike generic adaptation methods that rely on global feature alignment or dense pseudo-labeling, ForestPlotUDA explicitly targets the severe class imbalance and plot-wise structural variability inherent in forest environments, where ecologically critical woody components are sparsely distributed and easily overwhelmed by dominant foliage points. The proposed framework integrates decoupled feature normalization and class-guided self-training, enabling stable cross-domain adaptation under highly imbalanced and sparse supervision. Experimental results on the FOR-instance benchmark demonstrate that ForestPlotUDA improves the mean intersection-over-union (mIoU) from 54.71% to 61.50%. Notably, using only five pseudo-labeled points per class, the intersection-over-union (IoU) of the challenging wood class increases from 22.82% to 40.90%, highlighting the effectiveness of the proposed approach for annotation-free forest UAV LiDAR analysis. Additional experiments on SegmentedForests further demonstrate that ForestPlotUDA consistently improves over direct synthetic-to-real (Syn2real) transfer on ground-based terrestrial laser scanning (TLS)/mobile laser scanning (MLS) forest point clouds. These results indicate that explicitly accounting for structural heterogeneity and class imbalance is critical for Syn2Real adaptation in forest point clouds, paving the way for fully automated and low-cost forest inventory systems across diverse forest ecosystems.
author: Jing Liu, Jing Huang, Di Wang

title: Infrared Small Target Detection With Learnable Frequency-Domain Reconstruction and Explicit Redundancy Suppression
content: With the advancement of deep learning and object detectors, research on infrared small target detection (ISTD) has achieved notable progress. However, infrared small targets are affected by interference from complex backgrounds, which can easily introduce redundant background information during multiscale fusion, causing background and target features to mix indistinguishably and exacerbating the detection difficulty. To address these issues, we propose LFENet, a novel, end-to-end ISTD network with learnable frequency-domain reconstruction and explicit redundancy suppression. In particular, to mitigate target features being overwhelmed by complex backgrounds, we propose the C2f with parallel optimization (CPO) module. The module adopts a dual-branch attention with different pooling operations to separately model global background distributions and local target details, thereby enhancing target representation. To improve feature representation under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions, we introduce the clustered semantic attention (CSA) module, which adaptively constructs global semantic centers through iterative clustering to drive attention computation, thereby achieving efficient global modeling and feature enhancement. To address the feature mixing caused by redundant information during feature fusion, we propose the redundancy suppression feature fusion (RSFF) module. RSFF employs a learnable frequency-constrained upsampling operator for precise multiscale alignment and explicitly suppresses background redundancy during fusion, thereby enhancing the distinction of tiny targets from distracting noise. Finally, we introduce a Gaussian regression consistency (GRC) loss to stabilize localization by jointly modeling positional and distribution constraints. Experiments on public datasets demonstrate that LFENet outperforms state-of-the-art methods.
author: Bin Xiao, Yue Hu

title: A Physics-Guided Reconstruction and Injection Framework With Semantic Consistency Constraints for Oriented SAR Target Detection
content: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) target detection is pivotal for a wide range of applications, including maritime surveillance, reconnaissance, and strategic security. However, complex scattering mechanisms often render SAR targets discrete and discontinuous, leading to severe missed detections and false alarms. To address this, this article proposes the physics-guided reconstruction and injection framework (PRIF), which introduces the attributed scattering center (ASC) model to characterize these discrete physical scattering properties. The framework comprises the topology-guided semantic consistency matching (TSCM) module, the part-aware label assignment (PALA) strategy, and the physics-guided reconstruction and injection network (PRI-Net). Specifically, the TSCM module ensures the semantic consistency of physical parts by resolving the label permutation problem in clustering, while the PALA strategy effectively mitigates the scattering voids issue by achieving spatial alignment between sampling points and physical entities. The core architecture, PRI-Net, effectively boosts part-level local feature discrimination and significantly improves model interpretability. It achieves this by internalizing physical priors into feature representations through the physics-guided progressive reconstruction branch (PPRB) and performing explicit feature injection via the decoupled spatial attention mechanism of the physics-injected dual-drive detection branch (PDDB). The experimental results on the FAIR-CSAR dataset demonstrate that PRIF achieves an mAP50 of 0.468 and an  $F1$ -score of 0.547, significantly outperforming existing state-of-the-art detectors. Furthermore, cross-dataset validation on the RSAR dataset and portability experiments on baseline models demonstrate its robust generalization capabilities and plug-and-play characteristics.
author: Peng Wang, Yufeng Tang, Boao Qin, Daiyin Zhu

title: Physics-Consistent GPR Inversion via Feature-Enhanced Forward Module and Envelope Data
content: While full-waveform inversion (FWI) offers high-resolution ground penetrating radar (GPR) imaging, it is hampered by prohibitive computational costs and intrinsic sensitivity to initial models. Conversely, deep learning provides efficiency but often lacks physical constraints, leading to structural artifacts under noise. To reconcile high fidelity and robustness with computational efficiency, we propose a physics-consistent inversion framework driven by envelope data and a feature-enhanced forward module. A key innovation of our approach is shifting physical constraints from the noisy pixel domain to the robust latent feature manifold. Specifically, we construct a pretrained differentiable forward modeling engine and introduce a Latent Feature Injection mechanism. This strategy transfers multiscale structural semantics from the inversion network to the forward engine, enforcing strict physical compliance guided by the global geological context. This effectively compensates for the information bottleneck in traditional parameter prediction. Extensive experiments on synthetic and measured datasets demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms traditional baselines while maintaining the computational efficiency of deep learning. It exhibits superior inversion accuracy, robust noise immunity, and strong generalization capabilities.
author: Meijia Huang, Xiang Qiu, Yanqi Wu, Yonghao Wang, Zhuo Jia

title: Topographic Delays Correction Based on Optimal Selection of Common-Reference Interferometric Subsets
content: Tropospheric delays constitute the principal error source in the inversion of surface deformation using Interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) techniques. Here, a novel method is proposed to estimate the tropospheric delays and improve the accuracy of deformation inversion. First, a small baseline subset (SBAS) is divided into several common-reference interferometric subsets (CRISs). Subsequently, the CRISs optimally selected by a lookup table were employed to construct an inversion model based on the spatiotemporal distribution characteristics of tropospheric delays. The lookup table was constructed through 540 000 simulation tests. Finally, the estimated tropospheric delays are applied to correct the interferograms, enabling high-accuracy deformation inversion. The performance of the new method was validated through simulated and real tests. The simulation results indicate that the new method accurately estimates tropospheric delays with an average RMSE of 2.4 mm while achieving reductions of 56% and 62% in deformation RMSE compared to two commonly used methods. A real-world validation in Southern California confirms that the new method achieves an improvement of 29%–69% in deformation accuracy over four commonly used methods. Furthermore, validation on the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau demonstrates that the new strategy can correct the tropospheric delays of co-seismic interferograms with small-to-moderate magnitude earthquakes, enabling the accurate extraction of centimeter- to subcentimeter-scale deformation fields.
author: Guangrong Li, Chaoying Zhao, Zhong Lu, Baohang Wang, Ming Yan, Liquan Chen, Jianqi Lou

title: Differential Calibration of Satellite Altimeters Using Corner Reflectors
content: Precise assessment of satellite altimeter performance is essential to understand and monitor global sea level rise with confidence. This investigation introduces a new approach based on at least two co-located point targets called differential range calibration (DiRaC), which monitors the performance of satellite altimeters. By analyzing differential biases between point targets, DiRaC mitigates common errors (e.g., those related to atmospheric effects, geophysical corrections, and orbit inaccuracies) that affect absolute range calibration. The methodology is demonstrated using two rectangular corner reflectors (CRs) deployed at a dedicated calibration site (called ALX) in Crete, Greece, under the framework of European Space Agency’s (ESA) Permanent Facility for Altimetry Calibration (PFAC). Fully focused synthetic aperture radar (FF-SAR) processing is applied to isolate the radar returns of each reflector, enabling both absolute range bias estimation for Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich (Sentinel-6 MF) and the application of DiRaC. An initial assessment revealed a variability of 6 mm in differential range bias, which, given the current sample size, corresponds to an estimated standard error of 1 mm. This variability is attributed to the combined effect of the intrinsic altimeter precision and a processing-related correlated component. A quantitative assessment of the individual contribution of these two effects requires an accurate characterization of the processing-related correlated component. Hence, with an additional correlation analysis, the standard error of 1 mm can be more accurately attributed to the Sentinel-6 MF altimeter performance.
author: Costas Kokolakis, Dimitrios Piretzidis, Stelios P. Mertikas, Craig J. Donlon

title: A Physics-Constrained Deep Learning Framework With GAN-Based Data Augmentation for FY-3G MWRI-RM Precipitation Retrieval
content: Precipitation is a key component of the global water cycle, and spaceborne passive microwave remote sensing is one of the main means for global precipitation monitoring. This article proposes a semiempirical and semiphysical precipitation retrieval framework for FengYun-3G (FY-3G) Microwave Radiance Imager-Rainfall Measurement (MWRI-RM) that integrates stepwise physical mechanisms with the advantages of deep learning. First, observed data and precipitation samples generated by generative adversarial networks (GANs) are used to correct and augment numerical weather prediction (NWP) forecast fields, thereby constructing a “hydrometeor–brightness temperature” dataset that is physically distribution-consistent and class-balanced. Second, during retrieval, brightness temperature channel and polarization differences as well as precipitation type are introduced as physical constraints. A back-propagation (BP) neural network and an AttentiveRainNet model are developed to independently retrieve three hydrometeor parameters (cloud water, rain water, and graupel), explicitly resolving the “cold cloud–warm cloud” structure of precipitation systems. The surface rain rate is finally obtained through fusion calculation. The retrieval results are validated using FY-3G MWRI-RM Level 2 (L2) products and Integrated Multi-satellite Retrievals for GPM (IMERG) global precipitation products. Results show that the retrieved rain rates over ocean and land achieve strong consistency with the L2 product (correlation coefficients of 0.911 over ocean and 0.784 over land). Compared with IMERG, the correlation coefficient and root-mean-square error (RMSE) are 0.681 and 1.909 mm/h over the ocean and 0.713 and 0.763 mm/h over land. Notably, compared with the official L2 products, the proposed framework reduces the RMSE by 16.1% over the ocean and 27.8% over land. Furthermore, for Liaoning rainstorm and two typhoon cases in 2024, the model achieves excellent retrieval performance with correlation coefficients of 0.816, 0.866, and 0.771, respectively.
author: Yiming He, Zhiwei Wu, Ke Chen

title: Geo-ΔSSM: Geometry-Conditioned Δ-Modulated Selective SSM Network for Hyperspectral and LiDAR Joint Classification
content: Hyperspectral imagery (HSI) and LiDAR-derived elevation data possess distinct and complementary characteristics, making their joint classification essential for precise land-cover interpretation. However, the intrinsic heterogeneity between high-dimensional spectral signatures and geometric structural priors hinders efficient cross-modal interaction. This phenomenon further exacerbates the difficulty in resolving boundary ambiguities, ultimately resulting in suboptimal performance in geometrically complex regions. In this article, a geometry-conditioned  $\Delta $ -modulated selective state space model network (Geo- $\Delta $ SSM) is proposed to solve these challenges. Our core motivation is to explicitly regulate the spectral modeling dynamics of the HSI branch using LiDAR-derived geometric priors at the parameter level. Unlike conventional feature-level fusion, Geo- $\Delta $ SSM injects LiDAR-derived geometry into the generation of the selective SSM parameters, including  $\Delta $ ,  $B$ , and  $C$ , constraining spectral propagation by object boundaries. To further address spectral redundancy and noise, a frequency enhancement module (FrEM) is constructed to fuse static spectral priors with dynamic geometric guidance in the Fourier domain. The whole structure utilizes a weighted dual-modal boundary-aware loss (DBAL) to penalize errors at both material transitions and elevation transitions. Experiments demonstrate that Geo- $\Delta $ SSM achieves superior performance on three public benchmarks, effectively balancing accuracy on minority classes and preserving fine-grained details. The datasets and codes are available at https://github.com/bourne159/Geo-SSM
author: Chengbo Yu, Wenbo Yu, Min Ma, Yi Shen, Liqiang Zhang

title: SFPNet: Sparse Feature Propagation Neural Network for Hyperspectral Image Classification
content: Feature propagation models, represented by graph neural networks (GNNs) and Transformers, have achieved substantial progress in hyperspectral image (HSI) classification. However, existing approaches typically suffer from one of two limitations: patch-based strategies restrict the propagation range and hinder the modeling of cross-patch dependencies, while the superpixel-based propagation often struggles to produce fine-grained pixel representations. To address these issues, we propose a novel sparse feature propagation neural network (SFPNet) framework, termed SFPNet, which couples a pixel-level sparse feature propagation network (PFNet) with a superpixel-level sparse feature propagation network (SFNet). Specifically, PFNet constructs a structured sparse neighborhood by leveraging spectral and spatial correlations among pixels, and models fine-grained pixel dependencies via an efficient propagation operator, whereas SFNet captures long-range superpixel dependencies through a propagation mechanism with decayed neighborhood aggregation and state preservation. To accommodate different application scenarios, we further develop two PFNet variants with fixed and dynamic propagation weights, and couple each of them with SFNet to form two SFPNet architectures, namely, SFPNet-F and SFPNet-A. Few-shot classification experiments on six public benchmark datasets demonstrate that both SFPNet variants achieve consistently leading and robust performance across diverse distribution patterns and scale structures; compared with the best baseline on each dataset, SFPNet-F and SFPNet-A improve the overall accuracy (OA) by 1.98% and 2.25% on average, respectively. Moreover, modulewise ablations and spectral-domain analyses validate the strong fine-grained dependency modeling capability of PFNet-F/PFNet-A and the long-range modeling advantage of SFNet; operating under a unified sparse paradigm, the two modules exhibit clear complementarity, offering a generalizable design pathway for building efficient and robust feature propagation models for HSI classification. Our code is open-source on the public platform GitHub: https://github.com/LittleBlackBearLiXin/SFPNet
author: Xin Li, Xitong Xu, Shengbo Chen

title: BoostFormer-Based Dual-View Awareness Feature Fusion Classification for Hyperspectral Images
content: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and Transformers have achieved significant progress in hyperspectral image (HSI) classification tasks. However, most existing methods tend to process spatial and spectral features independently, making it challenging to fully model the multilevel spatial–spectral correlations, which limits feature representation capabilities. In response to this issue, this article proposes a BoostFormer-based dual-view awareness feature fusion classification (BF-DFC) for HSIs to extract spatial–spectral joint features. Specifically, in the spatial view, the spatial feature awareness (SpaFA) module efficiently captures local details and global context, while the Spatial BoostFormer (SpaBF) establishes local–global hierarchical correlations to enhance the discriminative power of spatial features. In the spectral view, the spectral feature awareness (SpeFA) module extracts local and global interactive information from the spectral domain, and the Spectral BoostFormer (SpeBF) further models the interplay of local details and long-range dependencies to improve the robustness of spectral features. Finally, the co-enhanced dual-view feature fusion (CoDF) module performs fusion of spatial–spectral features through cross-view interaction and an adaptive weighting strategy, further enhancing the model’s representation capabilities. Extensive experiments conducted on three hyperspectral datasets with diverse scenes and scales demonstrate that the proposed BF-DFC network consistently outperforms current state-of-the-art methods in classification accuracy with acceptable computational complexity. The source code will be available online at https://github.com/Yali-W/BFDFC
author: Yali Wang, Lin Zhou, Chuan Fu, Tan Guo, Yule Duan, Fulin Luo, Bo Du

title: Disentangle to Align: A New Paradigm for Robust Change Detection via Adversarial Feature Purification
content: Remote sensing change detection (RSCD) remains vulnerable to pseudo-changes caused by seasonal, illumination, and atmospheric discrepancies between bi-temporal images. Existing deep models often ignore this temporal distribution gap or align entangled features directly, which may corrupt change-relevant semantics and cause negative transfer. To address this challenge, this article proposes the disentangled adversarial alignment network (DAANet), establishing a novel “Disentangle to Align” paradigm and introducing a domain adaptation (DA)-inspired temporal distribution alignment framework for time-invariant feature learning (IFL) in change detection. DAANet first uses a content-style gate (CSG) to separate content-preserving features from style-biased residuals, and then applies adversarial alignment only to the residual branch. This targeted alignment encourages the backbone to learn time-invariant representations while preserving semantic cues for real changes. A dual-dimensional dynamic balancing strategy further stabilizes the adversarial optimization. Extensive experiments on WHU-CD, LEVIR-CD, SYSU-CD, and MSRSCD, together with backbone-universality analyses, demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of DAANet under complex imaging conditions.
author: Changxin Lu, Sijun Dong, Xiaoliang Meng

title: SCFDet: Selective Cross-Modal Fusion Network for RGB-Infrared Object Detection in Remote Sensing
content: RGB-infrared object detection in remote sensing is expected to enable all-weather robust detection by combining visible light texture information with infrared light’s thermal radiation properties. However, significant distributional and semantic disparities between the two modalities make effective complementary information integration difficult. Moreover, existing methods primarily emphasize cross-modal feature alignment or interaction and largely neglect the enhancement of the fused representations themselves. This oversight leads to underutilization of complementary information in fused features, ultimately hindering further improvement in model performance. To address these issues, we propose the selective cross-modal fusion network (SCFNet), a novel framework for RGB-infrared object detection that leverages a selective cross-modal fusion strategy. First, we design the selective mutual-guided feature alignment (SMA) module, which employs a bidirectional cross-attention mechanism for precise feature alignment, combined with a Top-K strategy to focus on salient regions. Second, we introduce the enhanced expert feature representation (EER) module, which utilizes a sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoEs) architecture to dynamically select optimal feature transformation paths, coupled with spatial attention modulation to enhance robustness. Third, we propose the cross-channel aware feature enhancement (CAE) module, which models channel-wise dependencies via consistency evaluation, amplifying semantically coherent features and suppressing conflicts. Extensive experiments on the VEDAI and DroneVehicle datasets demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance with 80.45% and 85.67% mAP50, respectively.
author: Fulin Luo, Yan Guan, Chuan Fu, Tan Guo, Zhixiong Nan, Tao Xiang, Bo Du

title: A PV Hot-Spot Fault Detection Network Based on Bi-Domain Complementary Distillation and Multiscale Feature Enhancement
content: The scale and distribution consistency of training samples are critical factors limiting the performance of deep learning-based detection networks. To address the scarcity of real-world photovoltaic (PV) hot-spot samples and the domain gap between synthetic and real data, this article proposes a PV hot-spot fault detection network based on bi-domain complementary distillation and multiscale feature enhancement (BCDNet). First, a dual-teacher distillation architecture is constructed to bridge the cross-domain gap by synergizing the precise geometric priors from synthetic data with the environmental robustness derived from real-world scenarios. An uncertainty-aware mechanism is introduced to dynamically guide feature alignment, thereby alleviating the domain distribution discrepancy between virtual and real domains. Second, to mitigate feature degradation caused by spectral aliasing during downsampling, a thermal-parametric wavelet downsampling (TPWD) module is designed, which suppresses background textures in the frequency domain to better preserve the spatial morphology of weak targets. Furthermore, a synergistic perception dual-stream (SPDS) module and an occlusion-aware detection head (SEAM_Head) are developed to dynamically enhance target saliency under strong interference. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves  $\text {AP}_{50}$  of 87.4%, which is higher than that of ten mainstream detection algorithms with only 2.6 M parameters.
author: Shuai Hao, Tianrui Qi, Xu Ma, Sirui Mao, Shiao Fan, Yimeng Cui, Keyu Hou

title: Physics-Informed Geometric Reasoning Network for Joint Cloud and Shadow Detection
content: Accurate detection of clouds and cloud shadows in optical remote sensing images is of great significance for extracting surface information. Despite the increasing maturity of cloud and cloud–shadow detection techniques, this task still faces certain challenges due to the complexity of the spatial distribution of clouds and their shadows. To address this issue, this article proposes a physics-informed space–frequency geometric reasoning network (PGNet). PGNet models the coupling between clouds and shadows through frequency domain consistency and spatial constraints, and improves detection accuracy by explicitly modeling displacement. A cloud–shadow spatial and frequency enhancement module is proposed to decouple radiometric intensity and structural information via discrete wavelet transform (DWT), and to enhance the physical coherence of cloud shadows through phase compensation in the frequency domain. A heterogeneous prototype graph geometric reasoning module is further developed to model the global topological relationships between clouds and cloud shadows via prototype learning and graph neural networks, enabling feature alignment under geometric projection constraints. A blind offset cloud–shadow completion module (BOGC-V) is introduced to reconstruct shadow structures and refine boundaries using physical displacement relationships, thereby improving representation in regions affected by noise. In addition, a geometric consistency loss is imposed to enforce physical constraints, ensuring coherent cloud and cloud–shadow predictions. Experimental results demonstrate that PGNet outperforms existing mainstream methods, benefiting from explicit physics-informed geometric reasoning.
author: Xinyu Cui, Bing Tu, Yan He, Bo Liu, Jun Li, Antonio Plaza

title: LapMDNet: Remote Sensing Object Detection Under Foggy Conditions via Physics-Guided Laplacian Prior and Masked Feature Distillation
content: For object detection in remote sensing images, foggy conditions tend to degrade image quality by scattering light and obscuring critical details, thereby compromising the performance of the involved detection models. To address this challenge, we first analyze the feature response of the Laplacian operation based on the atmospheric scattering model (ASM) and design two complementary Laplacian templates for bidirectional edge extraction and fuse them into a customized convolution kernel to enhance fog-degraded features. A rotated object detection method based on masked clean feature distillation is proposed, which leverages clean image features to facilitate the learning of fog-degraded image features. A dual-stream feature attention fusion module is then adopted to integrate the original yet blurred predistillation features with the clear but potentially noisy postdistillation features generated by the feature adjustment module, thus rendering the features for more effective object detection. Finally, a bidirectional attention-based feature pyramid network (BI-AFPN) is employed to enhance multilevel feature fusion. Extensive experiments on the dataset for object detection In optical remote-sensing images (DIOR)-Foggy, dataset for object detection in aerial images (DOTA)-Foggy, and real-world RDDTS fog datasets demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms other state-of-the-art methods.
author: Weizhi Yang, Jiangqun Ni, Yi Xie

title: Performance Assessment of the Vertical Wind Profile From Doppler Lidar Using Accumulated Spectra
content: Pulsed coherent Doppler lidar (CDL) is a remote sensing instrument widely used for measuring wind and turbulence in the planetary boundary layer (PBL). The CDL-derived vertical wind profile is typically obtained using the velocity-azimuth-display (VAD) algorithm. The quality of the VAD-retrieved wind field is highly dependent on the accuracy of the estimated radial velocities, which are a function of the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). The general trend of decreasing SNR with range often limits the maximum height of reliably retrieved wind profiles. To overcome this limitation, the maximum of the function of accumulated spectra (MFAS) technique was developed, where the wind field is estimated from a probability field derived from spectra of all azimuths. However, the MFAS-derived wind vector has only been quantitatively assessed using simulations. In this study, the MFAS-derived vertical profiles of horizontal wind vectors are validated against one month of radiosonde observations using the Wind Guardian-100 (WG-100) CDL, developed by the Metro Weather Company Ltd. The system was operated in a continuous plan-position-indicator (PPI) scanning, with range gates of 291 over azimuth angles at a fixed elevation angle of 60° at the University of Oklahoma. The observational comparison verifies that MFAS performs similar to VAD at a high SNR but can outperform VAD at a low SNR. Furthermore, a new metric, the accumulation quality index (AQI), is developed to identify reliable wind estimates in MFAS that are otherwise excluded by traditional SNR-based quality control. The simulation results indicate that the effective SNR extends to −34 dB, representing an improvement of approximately 3 dB over the traditional SNR-based quality control. In real measurements, the height coverage obtained using VAD is approximately 2 km on average. When applying SNR- and AQI-based quality control to MFAS, the retrieval range extends to approximately 2.7 and 3.4 km, respectively. The MFAS technique presents a promising opportunity to advance our understanding of atmospheric processes in the entrainment zone and the free troposphere.
author: Hsiu-Wei Hsu, Tian-You Yu, David Bodine, Joshua Gebauer, Junichi Furumoto, Kuniaki Higashi

title: Utilizing In-Orbit CYGNSS Roll Maneuvers for Improved Level-1 Calibration—Part III: Assessments of Nadir Observables
content: Improved characterization of cyclone global navigation satellite system (CYGNSS) zenith and nadir antenna gain patterns is incorporated into the calibration algorithms for normalized bistatic radar cross section (NBRCS) and reflectivity. The updated patterns result from work described in two companion papers (Part I and Part II). Calibration errors directly attributable to antenna gain patterns are reduced by 40%–90% across all nadir channels, while NBRCS consistency and uncertainty with respect to reference European Center for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts Reanalysis v5 (ERA5) data are improved by an average of 35%. Similarly, more than 80% of reflectivity measurements exhibit reduced uncertainty and improved correlation with coincident soil moisture active passive (SMAP) soil moisture measurements. The updated patterns also improve calibration consistency between satellites in the constellation, with a  $\approx$ 60% reduction in root mean square differences between them.
author: Mohammad M. Al-Khaldi, Scott Gleason, Christopher S. Ruf, Joel T. Johnson, Darren S. McKague, Anthony Russel, William L. Wells, Tianlin Wang, Dorina Twigg, Patrick McEnaney, Joshua Synowiec

title: GNSS-IR Snow Depth Monitoring Based on a PCA Optimization Framework: Considering Independent and Common-Mode Features
content: Global Navigation Satellite System Interferometric Reflectometry (GNSS-IR) has emerged as an effective noncontact technique for monitoring snow depth, a critical indicator of global climate change. However, heterogeneous topography and inconsistent surface reflectivity introduce spatial variability into reflected signals, significantly degrading retrieval accuracy. This study proposes a multi-GNSS optimization framework based on principal component analysis (PCA) that isolates the dominant common-mode signal from diverse observations, thereby effectively extracting true snow depth variations. The snow depths are retrieved from continuous multiseason GNSS observations at stations P351 and P676 and validated against in situ measurements. The results indicate that the PCA-driven method integrates the dominant common-mode information from multisatellite observations, enabling more stable snow depth time series across GNSS constellations. At station P351, the root-mean-square error (RMSE) of the original retrievals ranges from 18.2 to 25.6 cm, whereas the proposed method reduces it to 10.8–11.8 cm. At station P676, the original performance is substantially worse, with RMSEs of 33.9–47.7 cm, while the improved method reduces the error to 12.8–13.3 cm. The PCA-driven framework also effectively captures snow-cover dynamics, achieving its highest accuracy during stable snow-covered periods, with an RMSE as low as 4 cm. In addition, DEM analysis suggests that topographic differences are associated with substantial residual post-PCA biases. This indicates that the new method can, to some extent, mitigate spatial correlation errors associated with terrain variations and scattering characteristics related to the movement of reflection points. Overall, the PCA framework can more fully leverage the observational advantages of multi-frequency and multisystem data, thereby better exploiting the monitoring potential of GNSS satellites, and providing a reliable solution for GNSS-IR snow depth monitoring in complex environments.
author: Wenqi Liu, Kai Liu, Zhao Li, Xin Chang, Ran Lu, Qusen Chen, Weiping Jiang

title: Jointed AVO Inversion Method Using Seismic Velocity and Acceleration Signals
content: The seismic inversion is an essential step in reservoir prediction and fluid identification. Traditional prestack amplitude versus offset (AVO) inversion mainly relies on velocity signals. Although this technique is relatively mature, it suffers from low resolution and poor noise resistance under complex geological conditions. Moreover, the seismic inversion based solely on velocity signals is often insufficient to meet the increasingly demanding objectives of hydrocarbon exploration and development. This study proposes a joint inversion method integrating both velocity and acceleration signals. Based on the approximate expression of the Zoeppritz equations and the Levenberg–Marquardt (LM) algorithm, we construct an objective function for the two types of signals. To cope with the nondifferentiability of the LM algorithm at the zero point, we introduce the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMMs) to optimize the inversion process. The effectiveness and performance of the proposed method are then validated through both synthetic data and real data applications. The test results show that the joint inversion has significantly reduced the average relative errors in the inversion of P-wave velocity, S-wave velocity, and density compared to those from single-signal inversion. In addition, it exhibits stronger noise resistance. This joint inversion approach leverages the stability of low-frequency velocity signals and the high resolution of acceleration signals. Consequently, it yields more reliable results and provides a solid foundation for subsequent reservoir prediction.
author: Zhuo Lin, Ye Yang, Jiaqi Liu, Yuyong Yang, Zhengyang Wang, Kanglan Zhao, Huaibang Zhang, Huailai Zhou, Dan Chen

title: Localized Depth Estimation of Potential Fields by CWT Scalogram Analysis
content: Spectral analysis of potential fields, based on the Fourier Transform, allows high-resolution analysis in the wavenumber domain but not in the space domain. Because of this lack of spatial resolution, well-known methods, such as Spector’s and Grant’s methods, give information on the source depth but not on the horizontal source position. In addition, the estimated depth is often an average of the depths of different sources. Conversely, one significant feature of the continuous wavelet transform (CWT) analysis is that it has both space and wavenumber resolution. We propose to address these concerns by a CWT scalogram analysis obtained using a Morlet wavelet as the analyzing wavelet. In particular, we used a multidirectional Morlet fan, with  $n$ -fold symmetry. We show that it is possible to associate specific subregions of the scalogram coefficients to different sources, leading to a local implementation of the Spector and Grant spectral method directly within the 3-D CWT scalogram. This may be made by selecting specific subvolumes, 2-D sections, or 1-D profiles along the scale axis. Morlet wavelets with different central wavenumbers can be used to adjust the space and wavenumber resolutions differently: larger values allow for better wavenumber resolution, while smaller values increase the space resolution. We will demonstrate that both of these features are useful for performing a valid local spectral estimation. The method is tested on synthetic data, and it is also applied to the real aeromagnetic datasets of Mt. Vulture and NW Sardinia, Italy. For Mt. Vulture, we were able to compute the depth of intrusive rocks, lying from about 4- to 20-km depth. For NW Sardinia, we estimated the occurrence of intrusive volcanic rocks down to about 12-km depth.
author: Mahmoud Ahmed Abbas, Maurizio Milano, Ciro Messina, Maurizio Fedi

title: Ocean Rainfall Identification and Intensity Retrieval From GNSS-R Observations
content: Global navigation satellite system reflectometry offers a promising means for ocean rainfall remote sensing. Based on a spatiotemporally matched dataset constructed from cyclone global navigation satellite system forward scattering observations, GPM IMERG rainfall rate products, and ERA5 wind speed data, this study systematically evaluates five machine learning models (BPNN, Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost) coupled with the Optuna hyperparameter optimization framework and two data balancing strategies for rainfall identification. Using the optimal model identified, a rainfall intensity retrieval model is further developed and evaluated. The results show that for rainfall identification, the Optuna optimized XGBoost model with random undersampling achieves the best performance, attaining an accuracy of 95%, a Recall of 87%, an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.98, and a false positive rate of 3%, substantially outperforming existing convolutional neural network models under moderate to high wind speeds; for intensity retrieval, the XGBoost regression model achieves a root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 0.628 mm/h, mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.280 mm/h, and Bias of 0.010 mm/h, reducing RMSE by 22% and MAE by 10% compared with prior RF-based approaches. In addition, the proposed models demonstrate satisfactory spatiotemporal generalization across global oceanic regions. Limitations include degraded performance under light rainfall, extreme wind speeds, and heavy precipitation. Future efforts will focus on targeted model enhancements to address these scenarios.
author: Weiyi Deng, Qiushuang Yan, Jinpeng Qi, Chenqing Fan, Jie Zhang

title: Multistep Tunable Super-Resolution for Remote Sensing Image Clarity Enhancement
content: Recently, with the rapid development of deep learning technology, remote sensing image super-resolution (SR) reconstruction has become an important research direction in the field of computer vision. Traditional deep learning-based SR methods often suffer from oversmoothed reconstruction results and lack of high-frequency details. Subsequent methods have been improved to produce SR results that better align with human visual perception. However, these methods tend to introduce unpleasant artifacts into the reconstructed images. Currently diffusion-based approaches leverage forward noise addition and backward denoising processes to generate artifact-free SR images that also conform to visual perception. Nevertheless diffusion-based models still suffer from unstable SR performance. To address these issues, we propose a multistep tunable SR network named MTSR. Our network simulates the mapping process from low-resolution inputs to high-resolution outputs and introduces adjustable parameters. This design enables our method to produce nonsmooth SR results without artifacts while preserving rich and realistic textural details. Meanwhile, this study also optimizes the training network, enabling it to better capture the intermediate information transformations from low-resolution to high-resolution images. We conduct experiments on three datasets, and the experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves excellent texture recovery performance.
author: Guodong Ding, Jinhe Hu, Wei Xue, Dongxue Li, Peisong Jia

title: Infrared Small Target Detection Based on Multiscale Trilayer Local Statistical Difference
content: Current detection methods often struggle with serious false alarm residue and missed detections when extracting infrared small targets in intricate backgrounds. To solve this problem, a detection method based on a multiscale trilayer local statistical difference measure (TLSD) is proposed. First, the local statistical characteristics (including average, median, and standard deviation) between small targets and background clutter are analyzed from the perspective of a three-layer filter template. On this basis, a local difference measure (LDM) and a target likelihood measure (TLM) are constructed to reasonably represent the target signal. Subsequently, the TLSD is defined by integrating LDM and TLM, which can greatly reduce false alarms and enhance the target saliency. Finally, the multiscale calculation is used to extract infrared targets with different sizes in the image. Results prove that the algorithm can efficiently detect weak targets in complicated background, and it can achieve more robust and effective performance compared with existing algorithms according to visual and quantitative comparisons.
author: Yongsong Li, Yuezhen Jing, Zhengzhou Li, Abubakar Siddique

title: A Deep-Learning-Embedded Sparse Variational Optimization Method for Hyperspectral and Multispectral Image Fusion
content: Hyperspectral and multispectral image (HSI–MSI) fusion aims to reconstruct a high-spatial-resolution HSI by fusing an observed low-resolution HSI and a high-resolution MSI. While sparse variational optimization (VO)-based methods offer strong physical interpretability, their performance is often hindered by the limited representation capacity of hand-crafted priors in modeling complex spatial–spectral correlations. To address this, we propose a novel deep-learning-embedded sparse variational optimization (DLSpVO) framework. By formulating the fusion task within a spectral dictionary representation paradigm, we incorporate a dual-constraint mechanism for tensor coefficient estimation. Specifically, the tensor coefficient is parameterized by a deep neural network to introduce a deep implicit prior. Meanwhile, an explicit $\ell _{1}$-norm regularization term is imposed on the tensor coefficient to promote sparse representations that are consistent with the underlying linear spectral mixture model. To solve the resulting model, we develop a hybrid alternating direction method of multipliers-based algorithm. This optimization scheme seamlessly integrates a self-supervised zero-shot network initialization strategy to accelerate convergence, followed by iterative optimization of the deep network parameters and other variables. Extensive experiments on both simulated and real remote sensing datasets demonstrate that the proposed DLSpVO consistently outperforms state-of-the-art HSI–MSI fusion methods in preserving both spatial details and spectral fidelity. The source code will be made publicly available upon acceptance of the manuscript.
author: Wei Zhang, Liu Liu, Ting Xu, Liang-Jian Deng

title: Thin Cloud Removal From Remote Sensing Imagery Using Difference Map Supervision and Band Balancing
content: Thin cloud contamination constitutes a formidable barrier to the effective application of optical remote sensing imagery. Pixels that are affected by such contamination retain partial information, with thin clouds exerting differential effects across spectral bands. Motivated by these observations, we propose the difference map supervision and band balancing module (DBM), a lightweight external module for thin-cloud removal. DBM introduces a temporally adjacent auxiliary image into the multistage progressive image restoration network (MPRNet) backbone and regulates auxiliary-information fusion through difference map supervision and band balancing, resulting in DBM-MPRNet. DBM incorporates a difference map supervision module (DMSM) as the primary design and a band balancing module (BBM) as the complementary design. DMSM generates the difference map and transforms it into a learnable spatial gate to regulate auxiliary information along the spatial dimension. BBM dynamically adjusts the weights of the spectral bands during the training process to regulate auxiliary information along the spectral dimension. Through this cooperative design, DBM exploits reliable information from the auxiliary image while suppressing interference from erroneous information caused by temporal inconsistency. Extensive experiments on simulated and real-scene datasets demonstrate that DBM-MPRNet achieves significantly better quantitative and visual results than the baseline methods while maintaining a low computational cost. In addition, DBM shows strong robustness and maintains favorable cloud removal performance even when the auxiliary image is severely corrupted by noise. As a lightweight external module, DBM also exhibits strong transferability. When integrated into MemoryNet or MSDA, it significantly improves the cloud removal capability of the corresponding framework. These results demonstrate that DBM provides an effective and practical solution for thin-cloud removal in remote sensing imagery.
author: Kequan Pan, Zhongan Tang, Yiliang Wan, Feng Xu, Wenzhong Shi, Dizhou Guo, Yang Zhao

title: Dynamic Global–Local Selection Network for Hyperspectral Image Classification
content: The newly introduced Mamba architecture exhibits superior performance in the hyperspectral image (HSI) classification domain, as it achieves long-range dependence modeling with linear complexity and is widely regarded as a promising alternative to the transformer. However, existing Mamba-based HSI classification methods still face two major limitations: first, fixed multidirectional scanning paths lack content adaptability and introduce computational redundancy; second, the sequential scanning process disrupts intrinsic 2-D local structures, impairing fine-grained spatial features. To overcome these issues, we propose a novel dynamic global–local selection network (DGLSN), which synergistically integrates Mamba and a convolutional neural network within an input-adaptive multibranch framework. Our approach introduces two core modules: a global dynamic selection module that employs a lightweight decision network to activate only the most relevant Mamba blocks for efficient long-range modeling, and a local dynamic selection module that dynamically selects among spatial-, spectral-, and frequency-domain convolutional branches to extract discriminative multiview features. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DGLSN achieves state-of-the-art classification accuracy while requiring competitive training and testing times and significantly lower floating point operations, highlighting its superiority in both performance and computational efficiency.
